Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

areg

Regression absorbing one categorical variable

Stata 

areg y x, absorb(id)

R fixest 

fixest::feols(y ~ x | id, data = data, vcov = "iid", fixef.rm = "none")

Differs from Stata Absorbs id in OLS with conventional covariance; retains singleton groups as areg does.

Stata reference · R reference

avplots

Added-variable plots

Stata 

avplots

R car 

car::avPlots(fit)

Stata reference · R reference

bootstrap

Bootstrap standard errors

Stata 

bootstrap, reps(500): regress y x

R sandwich 

{ fit <- stats::lm(y ~ x, data = data); lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = sandwich::vcovBS(fit, R = 500, type = "xy"), df = Inf) }

Differs from Stata Fits OLS, resamples observation pairs 500 times, and reports bootstrap-covariance normal-reference tests. Random streams differ between R and Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

cluster

K-means clustering

Stata 

cluster kmeans x1 x2, k(3)

R stats 

kmeans(na.omit(select(data, x1, x2)), centers = 3)

Differs from Stata R defaults to Hartigan-Wong k-means and random initial centers; Stata initialization and iteration defaults differ. Control the starting centers to compare clusters.

Stata reference · R reference

didregress

Difference in differences (Stata 17+)

Stata 

didregress (y) (treated), group(id) time(year)

R fixest 

fixest::feols(y ~ treated | id + year, data = data, vcov = ~id)

Differs from Stata Group/time fixed-effect DID with group-clustered covariance. id is the treatment-assignment group; the coefficient is ATET only under the DID design assumptions. Stata diagnostics remain separate.

Stata reference · R reference

estat

Breusch-Pagan test for heteroskedasticity

Stata 

estat hettest

R lmtest 

lmtest::bptest(fit, ~ fitted(fit), studentize = FALSE)

These options match Stata's default test against the fitted values.

Stata reference · R reference

Information criteria

Stata 

estat ic

R stats 

c(AIC = AIC(fit), BIC = BIC(fit))

Differs from Stata Compare the same fitted sample and likelihood constants; R classes and Stata can count scale parameters and likelihood terms differently.

Stata reference · R reference

RESET test for omitted variables

Stata 

estat ovtest

R lmtest 

lmtest::resettest(fit, power = 2:4)

Stata reference · R reference

Variance-covariance matrix

Stata 

estat vce

R stats 

vcov(fit)

Stata reference · R reference

estimates

Keep a model for later

Stata 

estimates store m1

R stats 

m1 <- lm(y ~ x, data = data)

A fitted model is an ordinary object; keep as many as you like under different names.

Stata reference · R reference

Compare models side by side

Stata 

estimates table m1 m2

R modelsummary 

modelsummary::modelsummary(list(m1, m2), output = "markdown")

Stata reference · R reference

Store a model for a table

Stata 

eststo m1: regress y x

R stats 

m1 <- lm(y ~ x, data = data)

Regression table

Stata 

esttab m1 m2

R modelsummary 

modelsummary::modelsummary(list(m1, m2))

Table of the last model (Stata 17+)

Stata 

etable

R modelsummary 

modelsummary::modelsummary(fit)

glm

Generalised linear model

Stata 

glm y x, family(binomial)

R stats 

glm(y ~ x, family = binomial, data = data)

Stata reference · R reference

heckman

Heckman selection model

Stata 

heckman y x, select(s = z)

R sampleSelection 

sampleSelection::selection(s ~ z, y ~ x, data = data)

Stata reference · R reference

ivregress

Instrumental variables (2SLS)

Stata 

ivregress 2sls y x1 (x2 = z)

R fixest 

{ fit <- fixest::feols(y ~ x1 | x2 ~ z, data = data, vcov = "iid", ssc = fixest::ssc(K.adj = FALSE)); lmtest::coeftest(fit, df = Inf) }

Differs from Stata 2SLS with no finite-sample covariance multiplier and normal-reference inference, matching default ivregress 2sls. x1 is also an instrument for itself.

Stata reference · R reference

lincom

Linear combination of coefficients

Stata 

lincom x1 - x2

R marginaleffects 

marginaleffects::hypotheses(fit, "x1 - x2 = 0", df = df.residual(fit))

Differs from Stata For an ordinary lm, reports the linear contrast, delta-method SE and residual-df t interval/test.

Stata reference · R reference

logistic

Logit model reported as odds ratios

Stata 

logistic y x

R parameters 

parameters::model_parameters(glm(y ~ x, family = binomial(), data = data), exponentiate = TRUE, ci_method = "wald", ci = 0.95)

Differs from Stata Reports odds ratios, delta-method standard errors on the odds-ratio scale, normal Wald tests and exponentiated 95% Wald intervals, matching Stata logistic/logit, or defaults.

Stata reference · R reference

logit

Logit model

Stata 

logit y x1 x2

R stats 

glm(y ~ x1 + x2, family = binomial, data = data)

Stata reference · R reference

Odds ratios

Stata 

logit y x, or

R parameters 

parameters::model_parameters(glm(y ~ x, family = binomial(), data = data), exponentiate = TRUE, ci_method = "wald", ci = 0.95)

Differs from Stata Reports odds ratios, delta-method standard errors on the odds-ratio scale, normal Wald tests and exponentiated 95% Wald intervals, matching Stata logistic/logit, or defaults.

Stata reference · R reference

lrtest

Likelihood-ratio test

Stata 

lrtest m1 m2

R lmtest 

lmtest::lrtest(m1, m2)

Differs from Stata Compare the same fitted sample and likelihood constants; R classes and Stata can count scale parameters and likelihood terms differently.

Stata reference · R reference

margins

Predictive margins by group

Stata 

margins g

R marginaleffects 

marginaleffects::avg_predictions(fit, variables = "g", type = "response", df = if (inherits(fit, "lm") && !inherits(fit, "glm")) df.residual(fit) else Inf)

Differs from Stata For an ordinary lm or binomial/Poisson glm fitted with factor g: sets every estimation-sample row to each g level before averaging. Use g, since marginaleffects reserves the column name group.

Stata reference · R reference

Average marginal effects

Stata 

margins, dydx(*)

R marginaleffects 

marginaleffects::avg_slopes(fit, type = "response", df = if (inherits(fit, "lm") && !inherits(fit, "glm")) df.residual(fit) else Inf)

Differs from Stata For ordinary lm or binomial/Poisson glm: averages response-scale derivatives and factor discrete changes over the estimation sample; uses lm residual t degrees of freedom and GLM normal inference.

Stata reference · R reference

melogit

Multilevel logit

Stata 

melogit y x || id:

R lme4 

lme4::glmer(y ~ x + (1 | id), data = data, family = binomial(), nAGQ = 7)

Differs from Stata Random-intercept logit with seven-point adaptive Gaussian quadrature matches the default two-level melogit point count. Optimizer and quadrature adaptation can differ.

Stata reference · R reference

mi

Fit and combine models across imputations

Stata 

mi estimate: regress y x

R mice 

mice::pool(with(imp, lm(y ~ x)))

Differs from Stata Rubin pooling still requires matching complete-data degrees of freedom and small-sample adjustments to mi estimate.

Stata reference · R reference

Multiple imputation

Stata 

mi impute chained (regress) x1 x2 = y, add(20) burnin(10)

R mice 

{ impute_data <- data[c("x1", "x2", "y")]; predictors <- matrix(c(0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(names(impute_data), names(impute_data))); imp <- mice::mice(impute_data, m = 20, method = c(x1 = "norm", x2 = "norm", y = ""), predictorMatrix = predictors, maxit = 10, printFlag = FALSE) }

Differs from Stata Creates 20 chained Gaussian-regression imputations for numeric x1/x2 using each other and fully observed y, with 10 iterations. Explicit methods/predictors replace mice defaults; random draws do not coincide across programs.

Stata reference · R reference

mixed

Multilevel (mixed) linear model

Stata 

mixed y x || id:

R lme4 

lme4::lmer(y ~ x + (1 | id), data = data, REML = FALSE)

Differs from Stata Fits random-intercept Gaussian ML, matching default mixed rather than lmer default REML. lme4 does not add fixed-effect p-values.

Stata reference · R reference

mlogit

Multinomial logit

Stata 

mlogit y x1 x2, baseoutcome(1)

R nnet 

nnet::multinom(stats::relevel(factor(y), ref = "1") ~ x1 + x2, data = data, Hess = TRUE, trace = FALSE)

Differs from Stata Multinomial logit explicitly uses outcome code 1 as the base in both systems. Without the baseoutcome option Stata instead chooses the most frequent outcome.

Stata reference · R reference

nbreg

Negative binomial model

Stata 

nbreg y x

R MASS 

MASS::glm.nb(y ~ x, data = data)

Differs from Stata fixest::fenegbin() adds fixed effects. glm.nb() uses NB2 like default nbreg, but theta is the reciprocal of Stata alpha and likelihood/optimization reporting differs.

Stata reference · R reference

nlcom

Nonlinear combination of coefficients

Stata 

nlcom _b[x1] / _b[x2]

R marginaleffects 

marginaleffects::hypotheses(fit, "x1 / x2 = 0", df = Inf)

Differs from Stata For an ordinary lm with nonzero x2 coefficient, reports the ratio and delta-method normal inference, as nlcom. Ratios near a zero denominator are unstable.

Stata reference · R reference

ologit

Ordered logit

Stata 

ologit y x1 x2

R MASS 

MASS::polr(ordered(y) ~ x1 + x2, data = data, Hess = TRUE)

Differs from Stata Ordered logistic regression with ascending numeric outcome levels; coefficients follow the same cumulative-logit convention.

Stata reference · R reference

oprobit

Ordered probit

Stata 

oprobit y x1 x2

R MASS 

MASS::polr(ordered(y) ~ x1 + x2, data = data, method = "probit", Hess = TRUE)

Differs from Stata Ordered probit regression with ascending numeric outcome levels; check Stata numeric codes before converting value-labelled factors.

Stata reference · R reference

outreg2

Regression table in a Word file

Stata 

outreg2 using table.doc

R modelsummary 

modelsummary::modelsummary(list(m1, m2), output = "table.docx")

Stata reference · R reference

poisson

Poisson model

Stata 

poisson y x1 x2

R stats 

glm(y ~ x1 + x2, family = poisson, data = data)

Stata reference · R reference

ppmlhdfe

Poisson model with fixed effects

Stata 

ppmlhdfe y x, absorb(id year)

R fixest 

fixest::fepois(y ~ x | id + year, data = data, vcov = "hetero")

Differs from Stata PPML with absorbed id/year and heteroskedasticity-robust covariance, matching ppmlhdfe default covariance. Check separation, singleton removal and absorbed degrees of freedom.

Stata reference · R reference

predict

Fitted values

Stata 

predict yhat

R stats 

dplyr::mutate(data, yhat = stats::predict(fit, newdata = data))

Differs from Stata Here fit is an ordinary lm from regress. Predicts eligible rows outside the estimation sample too, as default Stata predict does. Other models require their own prediction scale.

Stata reference · R reference

2 more examples and alternatives

Predicted probabilities

Stata 

predict p, pr

R stats 

mutate(data, p = predict(fit, newdata = data, type = "response"))

Differs from Stata predict() depends on the R model: response/link scale, residual definition and prediction sample must match the Stata postestimation context.

Stata reference · R reference

Residuals for every row

Stata 

predict r, residuals

R stats 

dplyr::mutate(data, r = y - stats::predict(fit, newdata = data))

Differs from Stata Here fit is an ordinary lm from regress, so outcome minus linear prediction is the ordinary residual. This is not a generic GLM residual recipe.

Stata reference · R reference

probit

Probit model

Stata 

probit y x1 x2

R stats 

glm(y ~ x1 + x2, family = binomial(link = "probit"), data = data)

Stata reference · R reference

qreg

Median (quantile) regression

Stata 

qreg y x

R quantreg 

quantreg::rq(y ~ x, tau = 0.5, data = data)

Differs from Stata rq() default standard-error methods depend on sample size and can differ from Stata qreg; choose the covariance/inference method explicitly.

Stata reference · R reference

rdrobust

Regression discontinuity

Stata 

rdrobust y x, c(0)

R rdrobust 

rdrobust::rdrobust(data$y, data$x, c = 0)

Differs from Stata The R and Stata implementations share the estimator; version, bandwidth, mass-point and variance settings must also match for finite-sample output.

Stata reference · R reference

reghdfe

High-dimensional fixed effects

Stata 

reghdfe y x, absorb(id year)

R fixest 

fixest::feols(y ~ x | id + year, data = data, vcov = "iid")

Differs from Stata Absorbs id/year with conventional covariance. Check singleton removal and absorbed degrees of freedom against reghdfe.

Stata reference · R reference

regress

Linear regression

Stata 

regress y x1 x2

R stats 

fit <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data)

summary(fit) shows the coefficient table; broom::tidy(fit) returns it as a data frame.

Stata reference · R reference

5 more examples and alternatives

Factor variables and interactions

Stata 

regress y i.group c.x1##c.x2

R stats 

lm(y ~ factor(group) + x1 * x2, data = data)

Differs from Stata factor() plays the role of i.; x1 * x2 is c.x1##c.x2 and x1:x2 is c.x1#c.x2. factor() chooses its reference from R level order; Stata i.group uses its numeric base level. Set factor levels and contrasts explicitly.

Stata reference · R reference

Choose the base category

Stata 

regress y ib3.group

R stats 

lm(y ~ relevel(factor(group), ref = "3"), data = data)

Stata reference · R reference

Regression with sampling weights

Stata 

regress y x [pweight = wt]

R fixest 

fixest::feols(y ~ x, data = data, weights = ~wt, vcov = "hetero")

Differs from Stata For full survey designs with strata and clusters, see svyset. Match fixest covariance small-sample corrections and singleton handling with Stata; the same formula does not guarantee identical standard errors or retained observations.

Stata reference · R reference

Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors

Stata 

regress y x1 x2, robust

R fixest 

fixest::feols(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data, vcov = "hetero")

Differs from Stata Match fixest covariance small-sample corrections and singleton handling with Stata; the same formula does not guarantee identical standard errors or retained observations.

Stata reference · R reference

Clustered standard errors

Stata 

regress y x1 x2, vce(cluster id)

R fixest 

fixest::feols(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data, cluster = ~id)

Differs from Stata Match fixest covariance small-sample corrections and singleton handling with Stata; the same formula does not guarantee identical standard errors or retained observations.

Stata reference · R reference

rvfplot

Residuals against fitted values

Stata 

rvfplot

R stats 

plot(fit, which = 1)

Stata reference · R reference

sem

Structural equation model

Stata 

sem (y <- x1 x2)

R lavaan 

lavaan::sem("y ~ x1 + x2", data = data, estimator = "ML", meanstructure = TRUE, fixed.x = FALSE, missing = "listwise")

Differs from Stata Normal ML path model includes means and jointly modeled exogenous covariance, using complete cases. This matches the displayed simple sem model, not generic sem/gsem syntax.

Stata reference · R reference

test

Test a hypothesis about coefficients

Stata 

test x1 = x2

R car 

car::linearHypothesis(fit, "x1 = x2", test = "F")

Differs from Stata For an ordinary lm from regress, tests coefficient equality using its covariance and residual denominator degrees of freedom.

Stata reference · R reference

tobit

Censored (tobit) regression

Stata 

tobit y x, ll(0)

R AER 

AER::tobit(y ~ x, left = 0, data = data)

Stata reference · R reference

vif

Variance inflation factors

Stata 

vif

R car 

car::vif(fit)

Differs from Stata For ordinary lm numeric one-df predictors, gives the same VIFs. Multi-column factors produce generalized VIFs, unlike Stata column-wise estat vif.

Stata reference · R reference

xtabond

Dynamic panel (Arellano-Bond)

Stata 

xtabond y x, noconstant

R plm 

{ fit <- plm::pgmm(y ~ lag(y, 1) + x | lag(y, 2:99) | x, data = data, index = c("id", "year"), effect = "individual", model = "onestep", transformation = "d", collapse = FALSE); summary(fit, robust = FALSE) }

Differs from Stata One-step difference GMM: lagged y instruments from lag 2, differenced exogenous x instruments, individual effects only, and conventional GMM inference. The Stata noconstant option removes its additional level-equation constant; the displayed lag range covers panels shorter than 100 periods.

Stata reference · R reference

xtlogit

Conditional (fixed-effects) logit

Stata 

xtlogit y x, fe

R survival 

survival::clogit(y ~ x + strata(id), data = data, method = "exact")

Differs from Stata Exact conditional fixed-effects logit likelihood; unlike unconditional dummy-variable logit. id must identify the same panels.

Stata reference · R reference

xtpoisson

Fixed-effects Poisson

Stata 

xtpoisson y x, fe

R fixest 

fixest::fepois(y ~ x | id, data = data, vcov = "iid")

Differs from Stata Fixed-effect Poisson coefficients with conventional covariance, as default xtpoisson fe. Check zero-outcome panels and likelihood reporting.

Stata reference · R reference

xtreg

Panel fixed effects

Stata 

xtreg y x, fe

R fixest 

fixest::feols(y ~ x | id, data = data, vcov = "iid", fixef.rm = "none")

Differs from Stata Within-panel OLS with conventional covariance; retains singleton panels to preserve the xtreg sample. id is the xtset panel identifier.

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Panel random effects

Stata 

xtreg y x, re sa

R plm 

plm::plm(y ~ x, data = data, index = c("id", "year"), model = "random", random.method = "swar")

Differs from Stata Uses Swamy-Arora variance components explicitly in both systems. The Stata sa option is essential; default xtreg re uses a different estimator.
